While the checksum uses MD5 (less secure than SHA-256), it is still commonly used in AUR packages and, in this context, serves as a basic integrity check rather than a cryptographic guarantee. This does not constitute a security threat.

The listed dependencies are typical for a desktop application using GTK, WebKit, and system integration features (notifications, secrets, etc.). The package installation routine performs standard operations: creating directories under `$pkgdir`, moving desktop and icon files to appropriate system locations, copying application data, adjusting an XML filename in the appdata file via `sed`, and creating a symbolic link for the binary in `/usr/bin`. All actions are confined to the package build directory and the standard FHS paths, with no evidence of obfuscated commands, network access, or unauthorized file system operations.

There are no signs of malicious behavior such as data exfiltration, dynamic code downloads, use of `eval`, `curl|bash`, or other high-risk patterns. The optional dependency on `yt-dlp-git` is declared but not automatically installed or executed. The package follows typical AUR conventions for a `-bin` package and does not introduce supply-chain risks beyond the trustworthiness of the upstream binary — which is outside the scope of this audit.
</details>
